::: {.why}
You are about to build a data store, and every design decision in it follows from knowing what a daily bar is a summary of and what it destroys.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Say what each of open, high, low, close and volume is a summary of, and name one thing you cannot recover from the five of them.
- Explain why the close in your file may not be a trade that happened at a price anyone paid.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Take one liquid name and one day of one-minute bars, and reconstruct the daily bar from them. Check open, high, low and volume reconcile. Then say what the daily bar cannot tell you that the minute bars can: the path, the time of the high, the intraday range distribution.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} Compare closes across sources for the same five tickers on the same day: yfinance against any second source you have. Where they differ, work out which is the consolidated close, which is the primary exchange close, and which is the auction print.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Write the bar definition into the glossary, ending with the sentence about which of the five fields you would trust least and why.
:::
:::
